characters.summary: Achilles fights as an unmatched martial combatant and master of the sword and spear, relying on incredible agility, ferocity, and a reputed invulnerability that ends only at his heel.

mechanisms: Fabled near-invulnerability except for his heel

sources.supports: General character details, background, and portrayal in the 2004 film Troy.

feats.claim: Killed the giant warrior Boagrius in single combat effortlessly.
Slew Hector outside the gates of Troy and dragged his body behind a chariot.

notableResults.note: Defeated the champion quickly with a single sword strike.
Fought a prolonged duel outside the walls of Troy before prevailing.
Killed by a poisoned arrow shot to his heel by Paris.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of his mythical invulnerability are left unexplained in the gritty realistic tone of the 2004 film.

characters.summary: Agamemnon commands armies as a political and military leader, typically letting his champions like Achilles fight his duels while he directs strategy and commands troops.
weaknesses: Relies entirely on subordinates for personal combat prowess

sources.supports: Agamemnon's role as king and commander of the Greek forces in the 2004 film.

feats.claim: Conquered and subjugated various Greek city-states before launching the invasion of Troy.

notableResults.note: Political victory/dominance over Troy, though assassinated by Briseis later.

unknowns: Personal combat capabilities are limited compared to frontline heroes.

characters.summary: Agent Smith is a sentient computer program with superhuman physical capabilities, the power to overwrite human minds to clone himself, and complete control over the simulated physics of the Matrix.

mechanisms: Transferring consciousness to other agents or humans

weaknesses: Tied to the stability and rules of the Matrix system (initially)

sources.supports: Agent Smith's abilities, powers, and role in The Matrix franchise.

feats.claim: Dodged gunfire and exhibited superhuman strength capable of denting concrete and bending steel.
Overwrote the mind of Bane in the real world while possessing him via digital-neural interface.

notableResults.note: Destroyed when Neo unlocked his full One powers, though Smith returned as a virus.

campaignTags.claim: Can instantly relocate or possess other bodies within the Matrix network.

unknowns: Exact limits of his assimilation powers outside of simulated environments.

characters.summary: Al Powell is a desk-bound LAPD sergeant who provides crucial radio support, tactical updates, and firearms backup during crisis situations.
weaknesses: Psychological trauma from past accidental shootings

sources.supports: Al Powell's character details and role in the 1988 film Die Hard.

feats.claim: Shot and killed Karl Vreski to save John McClane at the climax of the Nakatomi Tower siege.

notableResults.note: Ambushed Karl with his service revolver to protect McClane.

unknowns: Not trained for high-intensity solo counter-terrorism combat.

characters.summary: Alexander Conklin is a high-ranking CIA black-ops director who manages elite assassins, utilizing surveillance networks, tactical teams, and operational authority.
weaknesses: Over-reliance on bureaucratic control and technology

sources.supports: Conklin's role as the CIA controller overseeing Treadstone.

feats.claim: Managed the global tracking and deployment of the Treadstone assassin network.

notableResults.note: Outmaneuvered and exposed by Bourne, leading to his downfall.

characters.summary: Andi is a local small-town resident/deputy context character who operates within police protocols and local terrain.

sources.supports: Context of local law enforcement officers in First Blood.

feats.claim: Participated in the initial local manhunt for John Rambo in the woods.

unknowns: Limited screen time and specific feat documentation.

characters.summary: Ardeth Bay is a Medjai warrior sworn to protect the world from Imhotep, skilled in horseback riding, scimitar combat, firearms, and ancient desert lore.
weaknesses: Standard human vulnerability to supernatural forces and conventional weapons

sources.supports: Ardeth Bay's background as a Medjai warrior and his combat skills.

feats.claim: Fought off hordes of mummified priests and undead attackers alongside Rick O'Connell.

notableResults.note: Defeated numerous undead ghouls using firearms and blades.

campaignTags.claim: Expertly fights while riding horses across desert terrain.

unknowns: Extent of survival skills against modern heavily armed military units.

characters.continuity: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (2005)
characters.summary: Aslan is a divine, colossal lion possessing immense supernatural strength, majestic presence, wisdom, and the power of resurrection.

techniques: Divine roars that shatter stone or paralyze foes

weaknesses: Bound by deep magic rules (willingly submitted to death on the Stone Table)

sources.supports: Aslan's attributes, magical abilities, and role in the 2005 film.

feats.claim: Overturned the forces of the White Witch and shattered her stone statues back into living creatures.
feats.citation: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (2005)

feats.claim: Resurrected himself from death due to the deeper magic from before the dawn of time.
feats.citation: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (2005)

notableResults.citation: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (2005)
notableResults.note: Rushed onto the battlefield and decisively turned the tide of war.

campaignTags.claim: Magnified magical lion significantly larger than any normal lion, towering over humans.
Wields powerful ancient magic capable of resurrection and turning stone back to flesh.
Restores injured or petrified creatures to life with his breath.

unknowns: Upper limits of his divine combat power when fully unleashed.

characters.summary: August Walker is a ruthless CIA/IMF assassin and operative who relies on brutal physical brawling, firearms proficiency, extreme endurance, and high-altitude infiltration.

mechanisms: Extremely high pain tolerance and physical durability

weaknesses: Arrogance and overconfidence in physical dominance
Standard human vulnerability to fatal injuries

sources.supports: August Walker's role as the primary antagonist and his combat feats in Fallout.

feats.claim: Fought Ethan Hunt in an intense multi-stage brawl in a public restroom and on a cliffside.
Piloted a helicopter in hazardous mountain terrain while engaging in aerial dogfighting.

notableResults.note: Defeated and pulled off a cliff edge by Hunt after a grueling struggle.

unknowns: Full extent of his underground syndicate network connections prior to exposure.

characters.summary: Azeem is a Moorish swordsman and scientific scholar who fights with an unconventional scimitar, advanced chemical explosives (Greek fire), and exceptional martial skill.

techniques: Creation and deployment of gunpowder/Greek fire explosives

mechanisms: Moorish lamellar armor and nimble parrying

weaknesses: Vulnerable to heavy armored knights in massed formations
Racial prejudice and hostility in medieval England limiting local allies

sources.supports: Azeem's background, combat style, and use of gunpowder/explosives.

feats.claim: Blasted open the gates of Nottingham Castle using improvised gunpowder explosives.
Defeated multiple Sheriff of Nottingham guards simultaneously with scimitar combat.

notableResults.note: Successfully cut through armed soldiers during castle infiltrations.

campaignTags.claim: Uses gunpowder and incendiary devices ("devil's fire") in combat.
Performs advanced battlefield surgery and herbal healing.
Creates gunpowder-based explosives and advanced tools in medieval England.

unknowns: Limits of his chemical formulas when exposed to damp weather conditions.
